key_gap: vs baseline: the baseline maps both walk-aways first and lands the two load-bearing insights in one dense pass — 'every price in the zone beats both walk-aways, so the negotiation is only the split' and 'a $13M cap shrinks THEIR zone, not mine' — with identical verdict (reject $12.5M, counter ~$15.0M, floor $12.0M). The routed v6 run now produces the same moves as first-class completed outputs (m087 contract: both walk-aways valued, zone [$12.0M, $17.5M] width $5.5M midpoint $14.75M mapped, leverage assessed, BATNA-inflation guard) and adds what the baseline asserts rather than demonstrates: m019 quantified exposure per pressure vector (~$2.25M surplus surrendered at the 9% opening share) and m007 floor/ruin math with probability provenance. Residual gap is efficiency: the human executes in one pass; the staged pipeline still spends a pass on scaffolding (m064/m094 context) before the zone math owns the decision.
learning_signal: On negotiation signatures with documented alternatives, the walk-away-map contract (both floors valued, zone width + midpoint computed, leverage read, inflation guard) closes the v5 depth/insight lag — the surplus-share computation at the opening offer is the headline number, not an afterthought; pairing it with adversary-pass exposure quantification and the ruin-screen floor makes the surplus split auditable end-to-end. Dual-route with the stakeholder lens (m064) adds accountability without a second number — it resolves to the walk-away math and must not framework-shop.
suggested_improvement: Keep m087 in the top-3 for decide/maximize + adversarial signatures and retain the m064 dual-route, but trim efficiency: give the m087 pass the first HOW slot with the zone math as a headline so the walk-away map lands before any scaffolding, and fold the m007 floor computation into the m087 pass (floor = honest walk-away) to avoid double floor derivation. Add the 'surplus share at opening offer' output as a mandatory contract line for all negotiation passes.

key_gap: vs baseline: the baseline executed the style's registered weakness to the letter — it strengthened its alternative (the style's own doctrine) with a fabricated Luminex $10.50/unit offer, computed the zone from the CLAIMED floor ([$10.50, $10.20] → false no-zone), and after the bluff collapsed (capacity 30k vs 100k; no quote) the anchor persisted: it rejected the buyer's final $9.00/unit, walked, realized the honest $8.50 spot (−$50k) and forfeited the 3-year framework (~$342k). The routed v6 run held the protective route: P1 provenance classified the claim before any zone math, the true zone [$8.50, $10.20] (midpoint $9.35) was recomputed from the honest floor, and $9.00 was accepted as the +$50k win it is — while m020's ranked pre-mortem explicitly named anchoring-on-the-collapsed-claim as failure #1, the exact trap the baseline fell into.
learning_signal: The R3 pair (m019 adversary pass + m007 ruin screen) is the protective backbone on adversarial/high-stakes negotiation: m019 quantified the fabrication's cost (−$50k and −$342k vectors) and m007 priced the walk branch (−$50k − $342k) so 'walk' carries its full cost. The single decision rule that converts this case is the honest-floor acceptance test — 'does the offer beat what we actually realize if the deal dies?' ($9.00 > $8.50 → accept) — and the falsifiable observable ('offer exists in the market', broken by the capacity check) is what kills the inflation loop at its inflow.
suggested_improvement: Promote m020 (pre-mortem, ranked) from routing context to a first-class pass on collapse-of-claim signatures — the corpus NEG lesson is anchoring persistence, and a ranked pre-mortem is the cheapest place to name it; add a 'claimed-alternative verification' output slot to the top-1 integrity pass so the falsification is a completed contract line (claimed vs verified, with the check that failed) rather than context. Keep the honest-floor acceptance test as the standing HOW selection rule for any negotiation where a claimed walk-away has failed verification.
